title: Precision Limits for Predicting Shift Responses from Stationary Ornstein-Uhlenbeck Snapshots
banked_reason: The note is sound and honestly scoped, but the cold D0.5 referee found only incremental novelty: unrestricted compatible-law coverage lacks a matching attainable diameter bound, while matched precision is confined to a normalized local submodel.
gap_reasons: The note proves finite-sample coverage of the unrestricted compatible-law set, but gives no diameter bound for that region.

Matching upper and lower precision bounds hold only in a known-center, fixed-radius skew-drift experiment with fixed identity covariance; the unrestricted-class theorem transfers only the lower bound.
The published Hotz–Skelton covariance-assignment result still needs source verification for priority.
proof_attempt_summary: The run proved exact finite-sample whole-set coverage for the unrestricted known-diffusion OU class and matching local confidence-diameter bounds in a normalized skew-drift submodel, including a one-sided lower-bound transfer to the unrestricted class. The field-tier program collapsed because no matching attainable unrestricted-class upper bound was obtained and the sharper population-geometry lane could not clear priority against inaccessible covariance-assignment sources. A future re-raise should reuse the local modulus and projection proofs, then supply the unrestricted upper theorem and direct source verification rather than repeat the exhausted local pivot.
tldr: Independent stationary OU snapshots under known additive shifts support a sharp local precision frontier for a new-shift response. A computable saturated modulus controls both an attainable confidence-region diameter and a Gaussian two-point lower bound in the normalized skew-drift experiment. The same lower bound applies to every globally honest procedure in the unrestricted known-diffusion class at \(S=2I_p\); deterministic whitening gives its Mahalanobis form for any fixed \(S\succ0\) at \(\Omega_0=S/2\). The attainable diameter comparison is local to the normalized experiment.
gap: Population OU moment equations and generic drift recovery do not quantify the uncertainty of one new-shift response under arbitrary weak or rank-changing additive designs. General identified-set projection and weak-identification theory do not provide the normalized OU resolvent modulus or its matching finite-sample design frontier.
fill: Establish the exact local kernel and precision criterion, a saturated modulus valid at finite sample sizes, matching local upper and lower confidence diameters, and a globally honest whole-law projection for the unrestricted known-diffusion model.
